text:
Priya Sharma: quick heads-up — noticed tail latency spikes for some tenants when requests get routed to int8 variants. thinking we should make quota tokens model-aware (tokens cost != latency cost).
Ethan Cole: +1. are these spikes from particular request shapes or general?
Priya Sharma: mostly long chat turns and streaming, but also bursts of short requests that fall back to slower runtime due to cold kv-cache.
Maya Lin: interesting. my suspicion: admission/credit system treats all tokens equal, so int8 vs fp16 imbalance causes unfair queueing.
Ethan Cole: would be helpful to quantify with a simple metric: token_latency_weight = p50_latency_per_token. then multiply credits by weight.
Priya Sharma: prototype idea: per-model weight + per-request shape multiplier. something like:
```
model_weights:
  gpt-small-int8: 0.6
  gpt-medium-fp16: 1.0
  gpt-large-q4: 1.4
shape_multipliers:
  short: 0.8
  long: 1.8
```
Maya Lin: looks reasonable. questions: where to compute weights? offline vs runtime? offline gives stability but misses hardware/context differences. runtime gives accuracy but overhead.
Ethan Cole: can compute baseline offline (perf profiles per region/hardware) and then attach lightweight runtime adjustments from recent 1m buckets. store as tags in routing config.
Priya Sharma: also need to avoid letting attackers game shapes. if someone pads requests to appear 'short' to get cheaper weight that's bad. need abuse detector signal integration.
Maya Lin: agree — we can ingest abuse_score from existing heuristics and apply a gating multiplier: if abuse_score > 0.7 then amplify weight by 2x or route to probation pool.
Ethan Cole: from infra side, we should keep admission API backwards-compatible: add optional fields {model_weight, shape_multiplier, abuse_factor} to the token request, default 1.0.
Priya Sharma: +1. I'll open an RFC sketch, but wanted quick team feedback: main tradeoffs = accuracy of weights vs complexity + attack surface.
rate-bot: deploy-check OK for config change to admission-api v1.2, flagged for canary.
Ethan Cole: also add observability: per-tenant effective_weighted_tokens metric and alerts for sudden drops/increases.
Maya Lin: and a canary rollout plan: start with non-critical tenants, run for 48h, compare p50/p99 and cost-per-token.
Priya Sharma: thanks — I'll draft RFC with sample canary plan and a fallback strategy to revert to flat tokens if regressions exceed thresholds. :thumbsup:
Ethan Cole: happy to review.
Maya Lin: will add abuse-detector integration notes.
Priya Sharma: filing RFC today, pinging folks when it's up.
